unitTitle: Deep Space Practice Mission: Reaction Telemetry & Mass Percentage Mastery
unitDescription: In-Session 90-minute flight telemetry challenge across 8 planetary sectors. Master metal reactivity, selective gas absorption, and mass percentage stoichiometry.
teacherNote: 🚀 Welcome to your 90-minute In-Session Practice Mission for 31/10/2026, Astronaut Cadet Keithley! 28 problems across 8 planetary sectors. Clean stoichiometry, zero simultaneous reactions. Keep your focus sharp!
assessmentTitle: Cosmic Chemistry In-Session Mission: Mass Percentage & Gas Telemetry (90 mins)
assessmentDescription: Timed celestial chemistry assessment with per-question chronometer controls. 100% English telemetry.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Reaction Recognition
questions.content_markdown: When dropping an asteroidal alloy powder composed of zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) into excess dilute sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), which chemical phenomenon occurs?

options.text: Only silver ($\text{Ag}$) undergoes reaction, evolving sulfur dioxide gas.
Only zinc ($\text{Zn}$) undergoes reaction, liberating hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2\uparrow$).
Both zinc and silver react vigorously with the dilute acid simultaneously.
Neither metal reacts; the powder remains completely inert in sulfuric acid.

questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Zinc stands before Hydrogen in the electrochemical series and reacts readily: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑. Silver stands after Hydrogen and remains completely inert.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Selective Gas Trap
questions.content_markdown: An atmospheric fuel sample containing ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) and ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is routed through a reaction chamber filled with excess bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) solution. Which statement correctly describes the gas retention inside the chamber?

options.text: The bromine solution is decolorized, ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is selectively absorbed as liquid $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Br}_2$, and ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) escapes.
Only ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) is retained inside the chamber.
Both gases are trapped and permanently retained inside the liquid chamber.
Neither gas reacts; both pass through the exhaust vent with zero mass gain.

questions.explanation: ANSWER A: Ethylene possesses a reactive double bond (C=C) and undergoes addition with Br2: C2H4 + Br2 → C2H4Br2 (liquid trapped in flask). Ethane has only saturated single bonds and passes out unreacted.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Mixture Mass Telemetry
questions.content_markdown: A planetary canister holds a total mass of $25.0\text{ g}$ containing aluminium ($\text{Al}$) and gold ($\text{Au}$). Spectral sensors reveal that the mass of gold ($\text{Au}$) is $15.0\text{ g}$. What is the **mass percentage** of aluminium ($\text{Al}$) in the canister?

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Insoluble Residue Principle
questions.content_markdown: A $15.0\text{ g}$ sample of metal alloy powder containing iron ($\text{Fe}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) is treated with excess dilute hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$). Following complete effervescence, an insoluble solid residue weighing $6.0\text{ g}$ is filtered out. What was the mass of iron ($\text{Fe}$) in the initial sample?
questions.explanation: ANSWER A: Copper stands after Hydrogen in the activity series and does not dissolve in dilute HCl. The 6.0 g insoluble residue is copper: m(Cu) = 6.0 g. Thus, m(Fe) = 15.0 - 6.0 = 9.0 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Solid Residue to Percentage
questions.content_markdown: A $25.0\text{ g}$ ore specimen containing magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) is reacted with excess dilute $\text{HCl}$. After the reaction ceases, an insoluble solid residue weighing $10.0\text{ g}$ is recovered. What is the **mass percentage** of magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) in the specimen?
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Silver does not react with HCl: m(Ag) = 10.0 g. The mass of magnesium is m(Mg) = 25.0 - 10.0 = 15.0 g. Thus, %m(Mg) = (15.0 / 25.0) × 100% = 60%.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Chamber Mass Gain
questions.content_markdown: An atmospheric stream of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is bubbled into a bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) absorption chamber. Telemetry reports that the chamber mass increased by $8.4\text{ g}$. How many moles of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) were present in the gas mixture? ($M_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} = 28\text{ g/mol}$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER C: The chamber mass increase is solely due to the mass of absorbed ethylene: m(C2H4) = 8.4 g. Therefore, n(C2H4) = 8.4 / 28 = 0.30 mol.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Dual Fuel Fractionation
questions.content_markdown: A $10.0\text{ g}$ sample of hydrocarbon gas composed of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) passes through a liquid $\text{Br}_2$ trap. The trap mass increases by $4.2\text{ g}$. What is the **mass percentage** of unreacted methane ($\text{CH}_4$) in the fuel mixture?
questions.explanation: ANSWER C: Trapped ethylene has mass m(C2H4) = 4.2 g. The unreacted methane mass is m(CH4) = 10.0 - 4.2 = 5.8 g. Thus, %m(CH4) = (5.8 / 10.0) × 100% = 58%.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Exhaust Gas Volume
questions.content_markdown: A $15.0\text{ L}$ stream of gaseous fuel containing $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is scrubbed through excess liquid $\text{Br}_2$. Exhaust sensors record that $6.0\text{ L}$ of gas escapes unabsorbed (measured under identical conditions). What is the **volume percentage** ($\text{\%}V$) of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) in the initial stream?
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: The escaping unabsorbed gas is methane: V(CH4) = 6.0 L. Absorbed ethylene volume is V(C2H4) = 15.0 - 6.0 = 9.0 L. Thus, %V(C2H4) = (9.0 / 15.0) × 100% = 60%.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Hydrogen to Metal Mass
questions.content_markdown: An asteroidal alloy containing zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) is completely dissolved in excess dilute $\text{HCl}$. The reaction releases $4.958\text{ L}$ of hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) at standard conditions ($25^\circ\text{C}, 1\text{ bar}$). What is the mass of zinc ($\text{Zn}$) in the alloy? ($M_{\text{Zn}} = 65\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Iron-Silver Separation
questions.content_markdown: A $14.0\text{ g}$ composite metallic sample of iron ($\text{Fe}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reacts completely with excess dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, evolving $3.7185\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas at standard conditions. What is the **mass percentage** of silver ($\text{Ag}$) in the composite? ($M_{\text{Fe}} = 56\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Trivalent Aluminium Ratio
questions.content_markdown: An alloy of aluminium ($\text{Al}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) is dissolved in excess dilute $\text{HCl}$, releasing $7.437\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions). How many moles of aluminium ($\text{Al}$) reacted? ($2\text{Al} + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\uparrow$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: n(H2) = 7.437 / 24.79 = 0.30 mol. By stoichiometric ratio: n(Al) = (2/3) × n(H2) = (2/3) × 0.30 = 0.20 mol.

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Aluminium-Silver Percentage
questions.content_markdown: A $10.0\text{ g}$ alloy specimen containing aluminium ($\text{Al}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reacts with excess $\text{HCl}$ to liberate $7.437\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions). What is the **mass percentage** of aluminium ($\text{Al}$) in the alloy? ($M_{\text{Al}} = 27\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Bromine Mass to Alkene Mass
questions.content_markdown: A gas stream of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is bubbled into a bromine solution until $16.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{Br}_2$ has been completely consumed. What mass of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) reacted? ($M_{\text{Br}_2} = 160\text{ g/mol}, M_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} = 28\text{ g/mol}$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: n(Br2) = 16.0 / 160 = 0.10 mol. Reaction: C2H4 + Br2 → C2H4Br2. n(C2H4) = 0.10 mol => m(C2H4) = 0.10 × 28 = 2.8 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Equimolar Fuel Canister
questions.content_markdown: An orbital fuel canister holds $0.20\text{ mol}$ of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and $0.20\text{ mol}$ of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$). What is the **total mass** of the fuel gas mixture?

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Equimolar Mass Fraction Principle
questions.content_markdown: For an equimolar fuel gas mixture containing $0.20\text{ mol}$ $\text{CH}_4$ and $0.20\text{ mol}$ $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (total mass = $8.8\text{ g}$), what is the exact **mass percentage** of methane ($\text{CH}_4$)?
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: m(CH4) = 0.20 × 16 = 3.2 g. %m(CH4) = (3.2 / 8.8) × 100% ≈ 36.36%. (While volume percentage is 50%, mass percentage is lower due to smaller molar mass).

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Magnesium in Noble Alloy
questions.content_markdown: A $12.0\text{ g}$ alloy specimen containing magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) and unreactive copper ($\text{Cu}$) is dissolved in excess dilute $\text{HCl}$, releasing $7.437\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas at standard conditions. What is the **mass percentage** of magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) in the alloy? ($M_{\text{Mg}} = 24\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Gas Split to Flask Mass Gain
questions.content_markdown: A $7.437\text{ L}$ (standard conditions) atmospheric mixture of $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is routed into a bromine flask. Sensors report that $4.958\text{ L}$ of unabsorbed gas escapes through the exhaust. By how many grams did the mass of the bromine absorption flask increase? ($M_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} = 28\text{ g/mol}$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Total moles = 7.437 / 24.79 = 0.30 mol. Escaping methane = 4.958 / 24.79 = 0.20 mol. Trapped ethylene = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10 mol. Flask mass gain = 0.10 × 28 = 2.8 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Reconstructing Initial Alloy Mass
questions.content_markdown: A planetary alloy containing zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) reacts with excess $\text{HCl}$. The process produces $4.958\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions) and leaves $7.0\text{ g}$ of insoluble silver residue. What was the **total mass** of the initial alloy? ($M_{\text{Zn}} = 65\text{ g/mol}$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER C: n(H2) = 4.958 / 24.79 = 0.20 mol => n(Zn) = 0.20 mol => m(Zn) = 0.20 × 65 = 13.0 g. Insoluble silver residue m(Ag) = 7.0 g. Total mass = 13.0 + 7.0 = 20.0 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Propylene Alkene Trap Fractionation
questions.content_markdown: An extraterrestrial gas mixture containing ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$, $M = 30\text{ g/mol}$) and propylene ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$, $M = 42\text{ g/mol}$) is bubbled through a $\text{Br}_2$ chamber. The reaction consumes $0.10\text{ mol}$ of $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ (chamber mass gain = $4.2\text{ g}$), while $2.479\text{ L}$ of ethane gas (standard conditions) escapes unreacted. What is the **total mass** of the initial gas mixture?
questions.explanation: ANSWER A: Trapped propylene: m(C3H6) = 4.2 g. Escaping ethane: n(C2H6) = 2.479 / 24.79 = 0.10 mol => m(C2H6) = 0.10 × 30 = 3.0 g. Total mass = 4.2 + 3.0 = 7.2 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Protocol Analysis: Magnesium vs Copper
questions.content_markdown: **Telemetry Evaluation:** Dissolving $12.0\text{ g}$ of a magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) alloy in excess dilute $\text{HCl}$ evolves $4.958\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions). An engineer asserts: *"Both metals react with $\text{HCl}$, and the mass percentage of magnesium is $40\%$."* Which evaluation is scientifically accurate?

options.text: The engineer's assertion is completely correct in both parts.
Flawed: Copper stands after Hydrogen and does not react; only magnesium reacts ($m_{\text{Mg}} = 4.8\text{ g}$), making magnesium $40\%$ and copper $60\%$.
Flawed: Magnesium is inert while copper produces all the hydrogen gas.
Flawed: Both metals react but copper accounts for $80\%$ of the total mass.

questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Copper stands below Hydrogen in the activity series and does not react with HCl. Magnesium reacts: n(Mg) = n(H2) = 0.20 mol => m(Mg) = 0.20 × 24 = 4.8 g (40%). Unreacted copper is 12.0 - 4.8 = 7.2 g (60%).

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Protocol Analysis: Zinc-Silver Stoichiometry
questions.content_markdown: **Telemetry Evaluation:** A $16.5\text{ g}$ alloy of zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) dissolves in excess dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, evolving $3.7185\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions). What are the correct stoichiometric moles of reacted zinc and the mass percentage of silver ($\text{Ag}$)? ($M_{\text{Zn}} = 65, M_{\text{Ag}} = 108$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Protocol Analysis: Hydrocarbon Absorption Check
questions.content_markdown: **Telemetry Evaluation:** A $9.916\text{ L}$ (standard conditions) stream of $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ causes a bromine flask mass gain of $8.4\text{ g}$. What are the respective molar amounts of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) and methane ($\text{CH}_4$)? ($M_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} = 28\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Protocol Analysis: Volume vs Mass Distinction
questions.content_markdown: **Telemetry Evaluation:** A gas mixture containing $0.10\text{ mol}$ $\text{CH}_4$ ($1.6\text{ g}$) and $0.30\text{ mol}$ $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ ($8.4\text{ g}$) has total mass $10.0\text{ g}$ and total volume $9.916\text{ L}$ (standard conditions). What is the volume percentage ($\text{\%}V$) versus mass percentage ($\text{\%}m$) of methane ($\text{CH}_4$)?

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • Quantitative Mission: Zinc-Copper Alloy Breakdown
questions.content_markdown: An alloy specimen weighing $15.0\text{ g}$ composed of zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) reacts with excess dilute $\text{HCl}$. The reaction produces $3.7185\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions) and unreacted copper residue. Determine the masses ($m_{\text{Zn}}, m_{\text{Cu}}$) and the mass percentage of zinc ($\text{\%}m_{\text{Zn}}$). ($M_{\text{Zn}} = 65\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • Quantitative Mission: Anhydrous Salt Telemetry
questions.content_markdown: A $10.0\text{ g}$ sample containing zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) reacts completely with excess dilute $\text{HCl}$, evolving $2.479\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions). If the filtered solution is evaporated to dryness, what mass of anhydrous zinc chloride ($\text{ZnCl}_2$) salt is obtained? ($M_{\text{ZnCl}_2} = 136\text{ g/mol}$).
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2. n(H2) = 2.479 / 24.79 = 0.10 mol => n(ZnCl2) = 0.10 mol. Thus, m(ZnCl2) = 0.10 × 136 = 13.6 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • Quantitative Mission: Aluminium Reconstitution
questions.content_markdown: A powder mixture of aluminium ($\text{Al}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$) is treated with excess dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The reaction produces $11.1555\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (standard conditions) and leaves $6.9\text{ g}$ of insoluble silver. What was the **total mass** of the initial mixture, and what is the mass percentage of aluminium ($\text{\%}m_{\text{Al}}$)? ($M_{\text{Al}} = 27\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 8: Neptune Frontier • Deep Space Gas Fractionation
questions.content_markdown: A $9.916\text{ L}$ (standard conditions) stream of fuel gas containing methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is passed through a $\text{Br}_2$ absorption chamber. The chamber mass increases by $5.6\text{ g}$. What are the volume percentage ($\text{\%}V$) and mass percentage ($\text{\%}m$) of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$)? ($M_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} = 28, M_{\text{CH}_4} = 16$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 8: Neptune Frontier • Dual-Phase Planetary Gas Cycle
questions.content_markdown: A $12.395\text{ L}$ (standard conditions) mixture of $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is scrubbed through liquid $\text{Br}_2$, causing a chamber mass gain of $8.4\text{ g}$. The entire volume of escaping unreacted gas is subsequently combusted completely in excess oxygen: $\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{t^\circ} \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. What volume of $\text{CO}_2$ gas (at standard conditions) is collected?
questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Total moles = 12.395 / 24.79 = 0.50 mol. Trapped ethylene: m(C2H4) = 8.4 g => n(C2H4) = 0.30 mol. Escaping methane: n(CH4) = 0.50 - 0.30 = 0.20 mol. Combustion of 0.20 mol CH4 yields 0.20 mol CO2. V(CO2) = 0.20 × 24.79 = 4.958 L.
